Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

stareal 0.2.0

Additive space-time components: main effects in space and time, random walks in time, and the four interaction types.

Additive space-time components

  • Main effects. fit_areal(main = ) adds independent main effects to the field: "space" (one spatial effect, the same at every time step, under the spatial prior with its own sigma_space and rho_space), "time" (one temporal effect, the same in every area, scale sigma_time), or "both". The default "none" is the model as before.
  • Random walks in time. temporal = "rw1" or "rw2" makes the time main effect a first- or second-order random walk, scaled so that sigma_time is roughly its marginal sd for any number of time steps; "ar1" (the default, with rho_time) is the stationary alternative. An RW1 sums to zero over time and an RW2 also has zero slope, so with the default ~ trend() the RW2 is the curve about the straight line.
  • Interaction types (Knorr-Held 2000). interaction = chooses the space-time interaction by whether its time and space factors are structured: "IV" (the default: AR1 x the spatial prior, as before), "III" (independent in time), "II" (independent areas), "I" (independent cells; use with nugget = FALSE) or "none".
  • Priors. areal_priors() gains sigma_space_sd and sigma_time_sd (half-normal, default 1) and rho_space and rho_time (Beta, defaults as rho_s and rho_t). fixed = accepts the four new hyperparameters, and spatial = "iid" or "icar" fixes rho_space as it fixes rho_s.
  • Everything downstream knows the components: predict() (Matheron’s rule with the main effects), crossval(), loo(), compare_models(), summary(), diagnose(), plot(), the checkpoint fingerprint, and simulate_areal(main =, interaction =, temporal =, sigma_space =, ...), whose $truth keeps the main effects.
  • The default model is unchanged: the same draws, predictions, cross-validation and leave-one-out scores as 0.1.0, bit for bit, and checkpoint folders written by 0.1.0 still resume.

stareal 0.1.0

The first numbered version: everything below, plus the 2026-10-28 changes.

2026-10-28: spatial priors, model comparison, group draws

  • More spatial priors. fit_areal(spatial = ) chooses the prior on the graph: "leroux" (the default, as before), "bym2" (Riebler et al. 2016: a scaled ICAR mixed with independent noise, with sigma roughly the marginal sd and rho_s the structured share of the variance), "car" (the proper CAR), and the shortcuts "iid" (Leroux with rho_s = 0) and "icar" (Leroux with rho_s = 1). All use the observed-cell machinery unchanged, so they cost the same to fit and predict. simulate_areal(spatial = ) draws from them too.
  • Fixed hyperparameters. fit_areal(fixed = list(rho_t = 0)) holds any of sigma, rho_s, rho_t and sigma_n at a value instead of sampling it, e.g. a field with no memory between time steps. Fixed values are left out of the draws, summary() and diagnose().
  • loo(): approximate leave-one-out cross-validation from one fit, with no refits. Each observed cell’s own latent value is integrated out before Pareto-smoothed importance sampling (Vehtari et al. 2016), which makes it stable where plain PSIS-LOO on this model is not. It returns a loo object, so loo_compare() works on it.
  • compare_models(): one row per fit of the same data, best first: the model, whether it passes diagnose(), the leave-one-out score with the difference from the best and its standard error, and, if given, crossval() scores. Its help page says why it does not use AIC, BIC or DIC.
  • Draws of aggregates. predict(group_draws = ) returns the draws of chosen groupings’ aggregates (group x time step x draw), the draws the summaries are made from, so changes between years, slopes over a window and contrasts can be computed draw by draw. keep_times = keeps those draws, and keep_draws, at chosen time steps only.
  • Groupings given at prediction time. predict(groups = list("country", zone = labels)) aggregates to a grouping that is not in the frame, without rebuilding the frame (or refitting).
  • What made a result. Fits, predictions, cross-validations and loo() results carry $version: the stareal version, its commit when installed from GitHub, the sampler version, R and the BLAS.
  • The default model’s draws are unchanged, bit for bit, and its checkpoint folders still resume.
  • Website. A new tutorial 4, “Choosing a model”: the five spatial priors, switching the nugget and the trend off, a fixed rho_t, and loo() and compare_models(), checked against tutorial 5’s cross-validation. Tutorial 1 gains changes between years and a grouping made at prediction time, from group_draws. The simulation tutorial (now 6) asks whether compare_models() finds the prior that made the data. The Method page covers every prior and the leave-one-out. The cross-validation tutorial is now 5.
  • Checked. Simulation-based calibration (data-raw/check_sbc.R, now for any prior) gives uniform ranks for every parameter under BYM2, the proper CAR, ICAR and a fixed rho_t. On simulated data, loo() agrees with exact leave-one-out (40 refits) to within 0.5 in total elpd, with cell-by-cell correlation above 0.999, in seconds instead of minutes (data-raw/check_loo.R).

2026-10-26: website

  • The simulated-data “Getting started” vignette is gone: the tutorials cover all of it with real data. “Get started” on the website now opens tutorial 1, and the notes on how cost scales moved to the Method page. For an offline tour, run demo("walkthrough", package = "stareal").

2026-10-26: percent, panel labels, progress

  • Prevalence is in percent (0 to 100) everywhere: predict()’s summaries and kept draws, plot(), crossval()’s observed and predicted prevalences (and so its RMSE, in percentage points), simulate_areal()’s true prevalence, and summary(fit, latent = TRUE). Exceedance thresholds are given in percent too: exceedance = 5 reports p_gt_5, the probability (0 to 1) that prevalence exceeds 5%.
  • Panel labels. plot(pr, ids = , labels = ) titles time-series panels with your own labels, one per id or named by id.
  • Progress from predict(). It reports the draws conditioned and predicted so far, with an estimate of the time left, in both phases and from parallel workers too.

2026-10-25: example data and the website

  • Example data. igad_crt76t holds 328 surveys of the chloroquine-resistance marker crt K76T in the eight IGAD countries, from the public STAVE collation. The surveys were selected by location, not by STAVE’s country names, which are unreliable. No boundaries ship with the package: the examples and tutorials download GADM with geodata::gadm().
  • Plots. plot(fit) shows every parameter of summary(), fixed effects included. Time-series plots of predictions (plot(pr), by area or group) add the observed prevalence of each surveyed area and time step, with its exact 95% binomial interval (data = TRUE).
  • Title. “Spatial-Temporal Areal Estimation from Survey Data”.
  • Borders that nearly touch. areal_frame(adjacency_snap = ) makes units whose borders come within that many metres neighbours. This is for boundary files assembled from different sources, which leave small gaps along national borders.
  • Folds of your own. crossval(folds = ) takes a fold label per observed cell, e.g. a country, for spatial cross-validation.
  • Comparing models. compare_cv() compares models cross-validated on the same folds, cell by cell, with the standard error of the difference.
  • Simulating at a real design. simulate_areal(cells = ) surveys the given area-time cells, with their numbers tested, so a simulation can copy a real survey design.
  • Fix: cross-validation log scores. The quadrature behind crossval()’s log score found the integrand’s mode by plain Newton steps. When a held-out survey was far from its predictive mean, these overshot, and the log score came out wrong by thousands (e.g. -18,698 for a survey inside its 95% interval). The steps are now damped. PIT, intervals and RMSE were not affected.
  • Website. Five tutorials (crt K76T by month, k13 R561H in East Africa, covariates, cross-validation, simulation), each running in minutes. The two long computations, the cross-validation of five models and a 20-replicate simulation study, ship with the package in inst/extdata/ and are imported by their tutorials.

2026-10-25: review and restructure

Interface

  • Simulations. simulate_areal() returns data ready to fit (a stareal_data with $truth), so fit_areal(sim) works directly.
  • Fit arguments. fit_areal(data, formula = ~ trend() + x, ...): formula replaces mean, and checkpoint_dir is now an argument of fit_areal() and crossval(). priors and control accept plain lists of just the settings to change, and fixed-effect priors can be named by design column.
  • Settings. areal_priors() and mcmc_control() return plain validated lists. In mcmc_control(), n_cores = 1 replaces parallel = FALSE, and verbose replaces progress.
  • Summaries. summary() and diagnose() return one class. diagnose() adds every observed cell, a check of the fixed effects’ ESS, and the verdict.
  • Prediction. predict(fit, groups = ...) replaces levels, and group tables are now under pr$groups. New: as.data.frame(pr) and sf::st_as_sf(pr, time = ...).
  • Draws. All posterior::as_draws_*() conversions work on a fit.
  • Time. time_frame(n_steps = ) replaces T, and its field is $n_steps. trend() runs from -1 at the first time step to 1 at the last, and is dropped when there is one step.
  • areal_data() no longer prints on assignment, and its surveys carry .id (the area id).

Sampler

  • The pseudo-data that steer the latent and hyperparameter moves are refitted at the chain’s mean during burn-in, then frozen. For rare outcomes this mixes the latent cells about 8 times better.
  • Chains start from dispersed points, so R-hat can reveal chains that have not mixed.
  • Seeds:
    • each chain and each prediction draw gets its own seed, drawn from the user’s, so any seed works;
    • results do not depend on the session’s RNGkind().

Running

  • Live progress. Worker processes’ progress now appears in RStudio, not only in a terminal.
  • Interrupts. On interrupt or error, the workers are stopped instead of running on.
  • Checkpoint folders. A folder is tied to its data, graph, model, settings and sampler version, but not to the R version.

Cross-validation

  • The log score integrates the held-out Gaussian exactly.
  • “Outside the 95% interval” uses a randomised PIT, so a calibrated model shows about 5% whatever the number tested.

Fixes

About 80 smaller fixes: input validation (factors, date-times, numeric ids, non-finite values, name clashes), memory bounds in prediction, messages, and documentation. See review_stareal-v0.1_2026-10-24.md in the source repository.
